stem: The student wants to contrast how fully the two programs covered their eligible populations, identifying each program by its delivery method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 2023, two neighboring counties offered free blood-pressure screenings to adults.
• Harlan County sent mobile clinics to workplaces.
• Harlan's program screened 6,200 adults, or 31% of the county's eligible adults.
• Reyes County set up booths inside pharmacies.
• Reyes's program screened 9,800 adults, or 14% of the county's eligible adults.
• In Harlan, 22% of screened adults were referred for follow-up care; in Reyes, 27% were.
choices: Reyes County's pharmacy booths screened 9,800 adults in 2023, whereas Harlan County's mobile workplace clinics screened only 6,200 adults.
Harlan County's mobile workplace clinics screened 31% of the county's eligible adults, whereas Reyes County's pharmacy booths screened only 14%.
In 2023, Harlan County screened 31% of its eligible adults for high blood pressure, whereas Reyes County screened only 14% of its own.
Of adults screened at Reyes County's pharmacy booths, 27% were referred for follow-up care, compared with 22% at Harlan's mobile clinics.
explanation: The goal has two conditions. First, it limits the contrast to how fully each program covered its eligible population. That is a share of eligible adults (31% versus 14%), not a headcount. Second, it asks you to identify each program by its delivery method (mobile workplace clinics, pharmacy booths). Only B does both: it names both programs by method and sets their coverage shares side by side with 'whereas.'

A.why: You saw that the goal is about reach and grabbed the choice that contrasts how many people were screened. Raw counts don't measure how fully a program covered its eligible population. Reyes screened more people but covered a far smaller share. This choice contrasts the wrong measure, so it points the comparison the wrong way.

C.why: You found the right attribute (share of eligible adults) and stopped there. The goal also asks you to identify each program by its delivery method, and this choice never mentions mobile clinics or pharmacy booths. It meets one of the goal's two conditions.

D.why: This choice names both programs by method and marks a contrast, but it contrasts referral rates, an attribute the goal never asked about. Referral rates describe what happened to people after screening, not how fully each program covered its eligible population.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a disadvantage of aerogel relative to mineral wool when the two materials provide the same insulating value. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Engineers compared two insulating materials for exterior walls: silica aerogel blanket and mineral wool.
• Aerogel blocks heat flow better than mineral wool does.
• To match the insulating value of a 1 cm aerogel blanket, a mineral wool layer must be about 2.5 cm thick.
• A 1 cm aerogel blanket costs about $40 per square meter; a 2.5 cm mineral wool layer costs about $5.
• Aerogel is brittle and sheds dust when cut.
• Mineral wool loses much of its insulating value when wet.
choices: For the same insulating value, an aerogel blanket needs to be only 1 cm thick, whereas a mineral wool layer must be about 2.5 cm thick.
For the same insulating value, an aerogel blanket costs about $40 per square meter, whereas a mineral wool layer costs only about $5.
Aerogel is brittle and sheds dust when it is cut, whereas mineral wool loses much of its insulating value when it gets wet.
An aerogel blanket is brittle and sheds dust when cut, and a 1 cm layer of it costs about $40 per square meter of wall.
explanation: The goal stacks three conditions. You need a disadvantage, not an advantage. It has to be aerogel's disadvantage relative to mineral wool, so both materials must appear with aerogel coming out worse. And the comparison has to hold at the same insulating value. B meets all three: at matched insulating value (1 cm aerogel versus 2.5 cm mineral wool), aerogel costs about $40 per square meter and mineral wool about $5. 'Whereas' and 'only' mark aerogel as the worse option.

A.why: You caught the 'same insulating value' condition and found the choice that compares the materials on that basis. But this comparison favors aerogel, since it does the job in less than half the thickness. The goal asked for a disadvantage, and this is an advantage.

C.why: This choice names both materials, gives each a drawback, and links them with 'whereas,' so it looks like a comparison of disadvantages. But it sets one drawback of each side by side instead of showing aerogel doing worse than mineral wool on a shared attribute. It also ignores the 'same insulating value' condition, and mineral wool's drawback could easily seem the more serious one.

D.why: Everything here is a disadvantage of aerogel, but mineral wool never appears, so nothing is shown relative to it. A $40 price means nothing as a drawback until you set it against mineral wool's $5 for the same insulation.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the force the two techniques require and to explain the reason for it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Relief and intaglio are two families of printmaking techniques.
• In a relief print such as a woodcut, ink sits on the raised surfaces left after the background is carved away.
• In an intaglio print such as an etching, ink sits in grooves cut below the plate's surface.
• A relief block can be printed by rubbing the back of the paper with a spoon.
• An intaglio plate must be run through a heavy press that forces damp paper down into the inked grooves.
• Both techniques were used to illustrate sixteenth-century European books.
choices: In a relief print such as a woodcut, ink sits on raised surfaces, whereas in an intaglio print such as an etching, it sits in grooves below the surface.
Whereas a relief block can be printed with just a spoon rubbed across the paper, an intaglio plate needs a heavy press to force damp paper into its inked grooves.
A relief block can be printed with nothing more than a spoon, but an intaglio plate needs a heavy press, and both techniques illustrated sixteenth-century books.
An intaglio plate such as an etching must be run through a heavy press, because the press forces damp paper down into the grooves where the ink sits.
explanation: The goal asks for two things: a contrast in force, and the reason for it. B sets the spoon against the heavy press with 'whereas', and it gives the reason the press is needed: the damp paper has to be forced into the inked grooves. Every other choice misses at least one of those two jobs.

A.why: You saw 'emphasize a difference' and picked a clean contrast with both items and 'whereas'. But this contrast is about where the ink sits, not the force each technique requires. That is the wrong attribute.

C.why: You found the right contrast, spoon against press, and stopped there. The goal also asks why, and this choice never explains why the press is needed. It spends its last clause on a similarity, the book illustrations, instead.

D.why: You were drawn by the explanation of why a press is needed. But only intaglio is described, so nothing is contrasted with relief printing and no difference is stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the drawbacks of the two cover crops differ. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Farmers often plant a cover crop after the fall harvest to protect bare soil over winter.
• Cereal rye survives winters well below −15°C.
• As cereal rye residue decays in spring, it can tie up soil nitrogen that young corn needs.
• Crimson clover adds nitrogen to the soil.
• Crimson clover is often killed by winters colder than −15°C.
• Both crops reduce winter erosion.
choices: Cereal rye survives winters well below −15°C, while crimson clover adds nitrogen to the soil in which it is grown.
As it decays, cereal rye residue can tie up nitrogen that young corn needs, while crimson clover adds nitrogen to the soil.
As it decays, cereal rye residue can tie up nitrogen that young corn needs, while crimson clover is often killed by winters below −15°C.
Because its decaying residue ties up nitrogen that young corn needs, cereal rye is a poorer cover crop than crimson clover.
explanation: The goal limits you to drawbacks, so each crop has to be represented by one of its weaknesses. C pairs rye's weakness (it ties up nitrogen) with clover's weakness (it can die in harsh cold), and 'while' links them as a contrast.

A.why: This contrasts the two crops, but on their advantages: cold tolerance and adding nitrogen. The goal asked for drawbacks.

B.why: This is the trap that survives the first insight. You noticed that rye's nitrogen problem is a drawback and that clover also involves nitrogen, so the contrast felt tight. But clover's half is an advantage. Only one drawback is compared, set against a benefit.

D.why: The notes never rank one crop above the other. This also mentions only rye's drawback, so the two drawbacks are not compared.

stem: The student wants to contrast how the mill printed its designs before and after 1834. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Harlow Mill printed patterned cotton in northern England from 1815 to 1870.
• Before 1834, its workers stamped each design by hand, using up to 12 separate carved blocks.
• In 1834, the mill installed an engraved copper roller that printed a full design in one pass.
• The mill's 1821 pattern book contains 40 designs.
• Its 1838 pattern book contains 310 designs.
choices: Before 1834, Harlow workers stamped each design by hand with up to 12 carved blocks; afterward, an engraved copper roller printed it in one pass.
The Harlow Mill's 1821 pattern book contains just 40 designs, whereas its 1838 pattern book, compiled after 1834, contains 310.
In 1834, the Harlow Mill installed an engraved copper roller that could print a complete cotton design in a single pass.
By installing an engraved copper roller in 1834, the Harlow Mill increased its range of designs from 40 to 310.
explanation: The goal is narrowed to *how* the designs were printed, which is the method. A gives the method on each side of 1834, hand blocks and then a single roller pass, and 'afterward' marks the change.

B.why: You correctly looked for a before-and-after contrast across 1834 and found one. But it compares how many designs the mill had, not how it printed them. That is the wrong attribute.

C.why: This describes only the roller, the after side. Without the hand-block method from before 1834, nothing is contrasted.

D.why: The notes give the roller's date and two design counts, but they never say the roller caused the increase. The choice also never describes the earlier method.

stem: The student wants to contrast the methods the two teams used. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Economists disagree about whether raising the minimum wage reduces employment.
• A team led by Ngozi Okafor phoned fast-food restaurants on both sides of a state border to count employees before and after one state's wage increase.
• A team led by Erik Lindqvist used payroll tax records covering every employer in that state.
• Okafor's team found no significant drop in employment.
• Lindqvist's team found a 1.5% drop in employment among teenage workers.
choices: Okafor's team found no significant drop in employment, whereas Lindqvist's team found a 1.5% drop among teenage workers.
Okafor's team counted employees by phoning fast-food restaurants, whereas Lindqvist's team found a 1.5% drop among teenage workers.
Both teams investigated whether one state's minimum wage increase reduced employment, though they gathered their data differently.
Okafor's team phoned fast-food restaurants on both sides of a state border, whereas Lindqvist's team used the state's payroll tax records.
explanation: The notes follow research order: question, method, finding. The goal points at the method stage. D puts each team's method on either side of 'whereas': a phone survey near the border against statewide payroll records.

A.why: This is a clear contrast between the two teams, but it is a contrast of findings, which is the wrong stage of the research.

B.why: This one survives the first check: it names both teams, uses 'whereas', and opens with a method. But the second half switches to a finding, so the two sides are not on the same attribute and the methods are never actually compared.

C.why: This says the methods differed but never says how. Stating that a difference exists does not emphasize what it is.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the difference in how well the body absorbs the two forms of iron to an audience unfamiliar with them. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Dietary iron comes in two forms.
• Heme iron is found in meat and fish.
• The body absorbs roughly 15–35% of the heme iron in a meal.
• Non-heme iron is found in plant foods such as lentils and spinach.
• The body absorbs roughly 2–20% of the non-heme iron in a meal.
• Eating vitamin C in the same meal can raise non-heme iron absorption.
choices: The body absorbs roughly 15–35% of heme iron in a meal, while it absorbs only about 2–20% of non-heme iron.
Heme iron is found in meat and fish, whereas non-heme iron is found in plant foods such as lentils and spinach.
With vitamin C in the same meal, non-heme iron from lentils can be absorbed as readily as heme iron from fish.
The body absorbs roughly 15–35% of heme iron, found in meat and fish, but only 2–20% of non-heme iron, found in plants.
explanation: There are two conditions. The choice must contrast absorption, and it must tell a reader who has never heard these terms what each form is. D gives both absorption ranges joined by 'but only', and it identifies each form by its food source in a short modifier.

A.why: You found the right contrast and probably stopped. But 'heme' and 'non-heme' mean nothing to an unfamiliar reader, and this choice never says what either one is.

B.why: This explains what each form is, but the contrast it draws is about food sources, not absorption. The difference the goal asks for never appears.

C.why: The notes say vitamin C can raise non-heme absorption, not that it makes the two forms equal. The choice also suggests a similarity, which works against emphasizing a difference.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the cost-effectiveness of the two programs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A county tested two programs to raise flu vaccination rates.
• Mobile clinics visited 30 neighborhoods and gave 4,200 vaccinations.
• The mobile clinics cost $126,000, or $30 per vaccination.
• Text-message reminders were sent to 60,000 residents and led to 1,800 additional vaccinations.
• The reminders cost $9,000, or $5 per vaccination.
choices: Each vaccination resulting from the text reminders cost the county $5, compared with $30 for each one given at a mobile clinic.
The mobile clinics cost the county $126,000, while the text-message reminders cost only $9,000, a far smaller sum.
The mobile clinics gave 4,200 vaccinations, more than twice the 1,800 additional vaccinations that followed the text reminders.
Sent to 60,000 residents, the county's text-message reminders led to 1,800 additional vaccinations at a cost of $5 each.
explanation: Cost-effectiveness means cost relative to results, here the cost per vaccination. A puts both per-vaccination figures, $5 and $30, side by side and joins them with 'compared with'.

B.why: This is the second-order trap. You recognized that the goal is about cost and found a cost contrast. But totals ignore how many vaccinations each program produced, so they do not measure cost-effectiveness.

C.why: This compares reach, meaning the number of vaccinations, without any cost. That is the wrong attribute.

D.why: This gives the right measure, but for only one program. With no mobile-clinic figure next to it, nothing is compared.

stem: The student wants to contrast how the deck is connected to the towers in the two designs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Suspension and cable-stayed bridges both hold up a roadway deck with steel cables and towers.
• In a suspension bridge, the deck hangs from vertical suspenders attached to main cables draped between the towers.
• In a cable-stayed bridge, cables run in straight lines directly from the towers to the deck.
• A suspension bridge's main cables are anchored in massive blocks at each end; a cable-stayed bridge needs no such anchorages.
• The longest suspension spans exceed 1,900 meters; the longest cable-stayed spans are about 1,100 meters.
choices: Unlike a suspension bridge, whose main cables are anchored in massive blocks at each end, a cable-stayed bridge needs no such anchorages.
The longest suspension bridge spans exceed 1,900 meters, while the longest cable-stayed spans reach only about 1,100 meters.
A suspension bridge's deck hangs from suspenders on cables draped between towers, whereas a cable-stayed deck is tied to its towers by straight cables.
Suspension and cable-stayed bridges alike hold up a roadway deck by means of steel cables that are supported by tall towers.
explanation: The attribute the goal names is the connection between deck and towers. C describes each design's connection, suspenders on draped cables against straight cables running directly to the towers, and joins them with 'whereas'.

A.why: This is a real structural difference between the two designs, and it is about cables, so it feels close. But anchorages hold the cables at the bridge's ends. They do not connect the deck to the towers, so this is the wrong attribute.

B.why: This contrasts span length, an attribute the goal does not mention.

D.why: This states what the two designs share. The goal asks for a contrast.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the two teams' conclusions differed while noting that both teams studied the same fossils. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fossil seeds about 300 million years old have been found in the Verrin Basin.
• A team led by Folake Adeyemi measured the seeds' thick outer coats.
• Adeyemi's team concluded that the seeds were dispersed by water.
• A team led by Matthias Haas examined scars where the same seeds had attached to the parent plant.
• Haas's team concluded that the seeds fell close to the parent plant.
choices: Adeyemi's team concluded that Verrin Basin seeds were dispersed by water, whereas Haas's team concluded that Verrin Basin seeds fell near the parent plant.
Although both teams studied the same Verrin Basin seeds, Adeyemi's team concluded they were dispersed by water, while Haas's concluded they fell near the parent plant.
Although both teams studied the same Verrin Basin seeds, Adeyemi's team measured their outer coats, while Haas's team examined their attachment scars.
Studying the same Verrin Basin seeds, Haas's team disproved the conclusion of Adeyemi's team that the seeds had been dispersed by water.
explanation: The goal has two conditions: contrast the conclusions, and say that the teams studied the same fossils. B states the shared specimens in its opening clause, then sets one conclusion against the other with 'while'.

A.why: You found the contrast between the conclusions, which was the main insight. But this choice never says the teams examined the same seeds, so it drops the second condition.

C.why: This meets the 'same fossils' condition and has the right contrast structure, but it compares methods, not conclusions. That is the wrong stage of the research.

D.why: The notes report two conclusions that disagree. They never say that Haas's team proved Adeyemi's team wrong. This choice also gives only one team's conclusion.
